chunks: Al-Husayn b. Ibrahim b. Natana (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, from 'Ali b. Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad b. Abi 'Umayr, from Hamza b. Humran, who said: Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) said:

My grandchild will be killed in the land of Khurasan in a city called Tus. Whoever visits him there, recognizing his right, I will take him by my hand on the Day of Resurrection and admit him to Paradise, even if he were among the people of major sins.

I said: 'May I be your ransom, what is recognizing his right?' He said: 'To know that he is an Imam whose obedience is obligatory, a stranger, a martyr. Whoever visits him recognizing his right, Allah the Mighty and Majestic will give him the reward of seventy martyrs who were truly martyred before the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family).'

key_terms.زيارة: Visitation (ziyara) — pilgrimage to an Imam's shrine
key_terms.عارفاً بحقه: Recognizing his right — acknowledging his divinely appointed Imamate
key_terms.غريب شهيد: Stranger and martyr — describing Imam al-Rida who died far from home as a poisoned martyr
key_terms.مفترض الطاعة: Obligatory obedience — theological term for the Imam whose authority is divinely mandated

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about recognizing the right of Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) said: 'My grandchild will be killed in the land of Khurasan in a city called Tus. Whoever visits him there, recognizing his right, I will take him by the hand on the Day of Resurrection and admit him to Paradise, even if he were among the people of major sins.' The narrator asked: 'May I be your ransom, what is recognizing his right?' The Imam replied: 'To know that he is an Imam whose obedience is obligatory, a stranger, a martyr. Whoever visits him recognizing his right, Allah the Mighty and Majestic will give him the reward of seventy martyrs who were truly martyred before the Messenger of Allah.' This hadith defines the theological prerequisites for a valid ziyara.
